rules.title: Potential personal-data field
rules.reasoning: A schema, model, or request-handling expression appears to represent personal data. A field name is an indicator, not proof of collection, identifiability, or a compliance violation.
rules.recommended_fix: Confirm what data is processed, document purpose and retention, and minimize fields that are not required.
rules.false_positive_notes: May describe test data, a non-personal identifier, or an unused field.

rules.title: Potential sensitive or special-category data
rules.reasoning: A schema or data-handling expression appears to refer to health, biometric, or another sensitive category. Context, purpose, and applicable law determine the significance.
rules.recommended_fix: Verify the data category and purpose; seek privacy/legal review and apply appropriate access, minimization, and retention safeguards.
rules.false_positive_notes: A keyword may be documentation, a test fixture, or a non-personal field.

rules.title: Potential SQL injection
rules.reasoning: Untrusted input appears to be interpolated or concatenated into SQL before execution.
rules.recommended_fix: Use bound parameters or the ORM's parameterized query API; do not interpolate untrusted values into SQL.
rules.false_positive_notes: Review whether the value is truly untrusted and whether a safe binding occurs in a wrapper.

rules.title: Potential hardcoded credential
rules.reasoning: A credential-like variable or assignment contains a non-placeholder literal value.
rules.recommended_fix: Revoke exposed credentials, rotate affected secrets, and load replacements from a secret manager or protected environment.
rules.false_positive_notes: Example placeholders and test fixtures can resemble credentials; detected values are redacted from the report.

rules.title: Potential sensitive-data logging
rules.reasoning: A logging call appears to include a request body, user object, credential, or personal-data field.
rules.recommended_fix: Log only necessary metadata; redact personal data and credentials, and verify log access and retention controls.
rules.false_positive_notes: The argument may already be redacted or may contain synthetic data; inspect the logger and data flow.

rules.title: Review authentication and authorization on personal-data route
rules.reasoning: A route appears to access or return personal data, but the scanner could not confirm an effective authentication and object-level authorization check from visible code.
rules.recommended_fix: Trace router and middleware dependencies; verify authentication and per-object/per-tenant authorization with negative access tests.
rules.false_positive_notes: Authentication or authorization may be enforced by middleware, a gateway, or a shared service not visible in this file.

rules.title: Review broad database result exposure
rules.reasoning: A route may return a collection or ORM/database result without an obvious response-field allowlist.
rules.recommended_fix: Use an explicit response schema or projection and confirm pagination, field minimization, and object-level access checks.
rules.false_positive_notes: The query may already be scoped or serialization may filter fields in a shared layer.

rules.title: Review bulk personal-data export
rules.reasoning: A route appears to export or download a broad collection that may include personal data.
rules.recommended_fix: Verify the export's purpose, authorization, field allowlist, pagination, audit controls, and protection of generated files.
rules.false_positive_notes: The route may export non-personal or already minimized data and may have controls enforced elsewhere.

rules.title: Review tenant scoping for data access
rules.reasoning: A route or query references tenant-scoped data without an evident tenant constraint in the analyzed function.
rules.recommended_fix: Derive tenant identity from a trusted authenticated principal and apply it to every read, update, and delete query.
rules.false_positive_notes: A repository, database policy, or middleware may apply tenant isolation outside the analyzed function.
